paragraphs.zh: Mesotrione, a potent and highly selective inhibitor of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPPD), is a member of the benzoylcyclohexane-1, 3-dioneherbicides. It has been widely used for the selective pre- and post-emergence control of a wide range of broadleaf weeds in the field of corn, seed corn, yellow popcorn and sweet corn. The structural formula referred to follows immediately as the page's only drawing, and a lone full stop is printed to the lower right of the drawing, closing this sentence. paragraphs.zh: Mesotrione possesses a broad spectrum of activity on various broad leaf weeds and grasses, for example, Abutilon theophrasti, Xanthium strumarium, Ambrosia trifida L, Chenopodium, Amaranthus and Polygonum species and Digitaria and Echinochloa species. Mesotrioneis useful in controlling weeds that are already present in crop by spraying, and controlling merging weeds by applying to soil. Various studies have shown that mesotrione does not show crop injury with pre-emergence and post-emergence applications and does not affect yield of crops at recommended doses.

structures.core: cyclohexane-1,3-dione whose C2 is joined through an exocyclic carbonyl (C=O) to a benzene ring
substituents: ketone C=O at C1 of the cyclohexane ring, drawn as a vertical double bond pointing up
ketone C=O at C3 of the cyclohexane ring, drawn as a double bond to an O at the lower right
the exocyclic benzoyl carbonyl attached at C2 of the cyclohexane ring, i.e. at the carbon between the two ring ketones; that carbon carries one implicit H
the exocyclic carbonyl carbon carries its own =O drawn vertically upward and bonds to the benzene ring on its right
NO2 at C2 of the benzene ring, i.e. ortho to the ring carbon bearing the carbonyl, drawn as the label NO2 on a bond pointing up from the top vertex

SO2CH3 at C4 of the benzene ring, i.e. para to the ring carbon bearing the carbonyl, drawn as a bond down-right to S, with two separate double bonds from S to two O labels and one plain bond from S up-right to an unlabelled line end (methyl)
no other substituent on either ring; benzene C3, C5 and C6 and cyclohexane C4, C5, C6 carry only implicit H
structures.name: 2-[4-(methylsulfonyl)-2-nitrobenzoyl]cyclohexane-1,3-dione (mesotrione)

drawings.notes: Single standalone structure, no arrows and no printed label or formula number beneath it. Read off the drawing at 7x magnification in two separate crops, one per ring. The benzene ring is drawn as a regular hexagon with a vertex at top and bottom; the carbonyl attaches at the upper-left vertex (C1), NO2 sits on the top vertex (C2), and the S sits on the lower-right vertex, which is the vertex diagonally opposite C1 and therefore C4, para to the carbonyl. Kekule double bonds are drawn on C1=C6, C2=C3 and C4=C5, a valid alternating pattern. All three positions were counted off the drawn vertices, not inferred from the name. The drawing AGREES with the name given in the prose of [003], '2-(4-(methylsulfonyl)-2-nitrobenzoyl) cyclohexane-1,3-dione', so nothing is recorded in discrepancies. presented_as is set to intermediate_structure only because the enum offered has no value for a standalone target-compound structure: this is NOT an intermediate and NOT a route. It is the structure of mesotrione itself, the final product of the invention, printed in the BACKGROUND section purely to define the compound. Do not read the enum value as a claim that this compound is an intermediate. The nitro group is printed as the label NO2 with no formal charges shown; the SMILES writes it in the charge-separated form [N+](=O)[O-], which is a convention of the notation and not something drawn on the page. SMILES was round-tripped through RDKit and is identical to the canonical SMILES of mesotrione, C14H13NO7S, MW 339.33.
